summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Located primary legal and analytical documents for Nepal's LDC-graduation preference changes: GA resolution A/RES/76/8, CDP monitoring and July 2026 crisis-assessment reports, WTO/EIF graduation-impact studies and the WTO-rule transition decisions (WT/L/1172, MC13), the new EU GSP regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1395), UK DCTS briefing documents, US NTPP law and reports plus the 2025 reciprocal-tariff orders, China's zero-tariff scheme for LDCs, the India-Nepal Treaty of Trade, Nepal's 2025 WTO Trade Policy Review and WTO tariff data. No values were retrieved; both research questions (preferences lost and timeline; tariff changes on top exports by market) remain pending. A preference-loss table skeleton and a tariff-change method are specified. Key open item: whether the GA has granted Nepal's 2026 request to extend the preparatory period, which changes the timing in scenario S08.

findings.claim: Preferences Nepal loses at LDC graduation, by market and scheme (EU EBA -> standard GSP/GSP+, UK DCTS Comprehensive -> Enhanced, Japan/Canada/Korea/China LDC schemes, US NTPP, India treaty unaffected) and the legal transition timeline for each.
findings.note: Requires `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` for the listed lead URLs, extraction of the named tables and ingest as observations in r2. Extract from A/RES/76/8, Regulation (EU) 2026/1395, UK DCTS rules, 19 USC 4454 and China CTC announcement.

findings.claim: Scheduled graduation date and whether Nepal's May 2026 request to extend the preparatory period has been granted by the General Assembly.
findings.note: Search results (not evidence) report a CDP crisis assessment (July 2026) and an ECOSOC recommendation that the GA decide before the scheduled date; the GA outcome was not located. Retrieve CDP crisis assessment, ECOSOC decision and any GA resolution; record as dated event observations.

findings.note: Retrieve 19 USC 4454 text, USTR NTPP page and 2025 Executive Orders' Annex I; record status as dated events. Legal status of IEEPA tariffs after litigation must also be verified from primary sources.

findings.claim: Changes in WTO-rule flexibilities at graduation (TRIPS LDC transition, SCM export-subsidy exemption, S&DT) and the transition granted by WT/L/1172 and the MC13 decision.
findings.note: Requires `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` for the listed lead URLs, extraction of the named tables and ingest as observations in r2.

findings.claim: Graduation affects only LDC-specific international support measures; the India-Nepal Treaty of Trade (bilateral, non-reciprocal) is not conditioned on LDC status and is treated as unchanged by graduation unless the treaty text shows otherwise (to be verified).

Where preference schemes differ in rules of origin (e.g. EU EBA vs standard GSP, UK DCTS tiers), loss of preference is measured on eligibility of tariff lines, with actual utilisation carried as a separate variable; utilisation below eligibility reduces the real impact.

Post-graduation scenario variants: (a) graduation on the schedule in A/RES/76/8 with standard transition periods; (b) graduation deferred per Nepal's extension request; (c) Nepal obtains EU GSP+; (d) Nepal does not obtain GSP+. No probability is assigned.

data_gaps: GA decision on Nepal's 2026 extension request not located.
National GSP legal texts for Japan, Canada, Korea, Australia, Türkiye, Norway and Switzerland (LDC tiers and graduation transitions) not located.
EU and UK preference-utilisation rates by HS line for Nepal not located (Eurostat/HMRC).
Post-graduation eligibility of Nepal for China's LDC zero-tariff scheme and any transition not located.
Current legal status of US NTPP after its statutory expiry and of US reciprocal tariffs as applied to Nepal not verified.
The session web-search budget was exhausted part-way through r1; further leads for this task must be located in r2 or by the orchestrator.

assumptions.text: Graduation affects only LDC-specific international support measures; the India-Nepal Treaty of Trade (bilateral, non-reciprocal) is not conditioned on LDC status and is treated as unchanged by graduation unless the treaty text shows otherwise (to be verified).

Where preference schemes differ in rules of origin (e.g. EU EBA vs standard GSP, UK DCTS tiers), loss of preference is measured on eligibility of tariff lines, with actual utilisation carried as a separate variable; utilisation below eligibility reduces the real impact.

Post-graduation scenario variants: (a) graduation on the schedule in A/RES/76/8 with standard transition periods; (b) graduation deferred per Nepal's extension request; (c) Nepal obtains EU GSP+; (d) Nepal does not obtain GSP+. No probability is assigned.

challenges.text: EXP-13 measurement should separate eligibility-based and utilisation-based preference exposure, and add a dated-event attribute for the GA decision on Nepal's extension request; also US exposure now depends on NTPP expiry and reciprocal tariffs, which are not LDC-conditioned and should not be counted as graduation effects.
Keep LDC-graduation effects (EU/UK/Japan/China LDC schemes, WTO S&DT) separate from non-graduation shocks (US NTPP expiry, US reciprocal tariffs) when attributing export changes in S08.
Escalation: if the GA grants the extension request, S08 timing and the transition-end years in the preference-loss table change; pending verification from CDP/ECOSOC/GA documents.
Escalation for red team: test S08 against the case where standard transitions apply on schedule and GSP+ is not obtained (strict case), and against concurrent US tariff changes.

uncertainty: High. All empirical items pending. Transition lengths and dates are known only from search snippets and are therefore not recorded. The GA decision on the extension request is unknown. Graduation-impact estimates in the WTO/EIF and ITC studies use older base years and may differ from current export structure; utilisation of preferences is unobserved so far.

preference_loss_table.method: One row per preference-granting market and scheme: current scheme, post-graduation scheme, legal instrument, transition length and end date, rules-of-origin change, eligibility of Nepal's top-export HS lines, GSP+/Enhanced eligibility conditions. Timeline fields populated only from retrieved legal texts.

graduation_timeline.open_event: Nepal's 2026 request to extend preparatory period (CDP crisis assessment July 2026; ECOSOC recommendation; GA decision not located)

tariff_change_estimates.method: Identify Nepal's top export HS6/HS8 lines by market from customs FY data (and partner mirror data, calendar year). For each line and market take (i) current applied preferential rate, (ii) post-transition applicable rate under the scheme Nepal would qualify for, and (iii) MFN; change = (ii) - (i) in percentage points. Weight by export value to get a trade-weighted tariff change per market; report eligibility-based and utilisation-based variants separately. Compare with WTO/EIF and ITC estimates and keep all values; explain differences (base year, HS level, utilisation, scheme assumptions).
tariff_change_estimates.products_to_cover: top export lines by market from customs data (expected to include textiles/garments, carpets, felt and pashmina products, travel goods, headwear) - list to be derived from retrieved data, not assumed
